title: Regularity and coordinate intersections on a permissible blowup chart
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] with a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$. Fix $1\le r\le d$, a nonempty subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with $J\cap\{1,\ldots,r\}\ne\varnothing$, and a subset $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$. For $j\in J$, the standard chart of the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] of the ideal $(t_i:i\in J)$ is
$$A_j=R[ u_i\mid i\in J\setminus\{j\} ]/(t_i-t_j u_i\mid i\in J\setminus\{j\}),$$
with $u_i=t_i/t_j$; it is regular. If $B=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$, the reduced inverse image [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] of $B$ on this chart is the union of the coordinate hyperplanes $t_j=0$, $u_i=0$ for $i\in(J\setminus\{j\})\cap\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and $t_k=0$ for $k\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\setminus J$. At every point these hyperplanes have local equations among a regular system of parameters; every intersection of a subset of them is empty or regular and has codimension equal to the size of the subset. If $M=V(t_i:i\in J)$ and $H=V(\prod_{i\in I}t_i)$ (empty product means $H=\varnothing$), the reduced inverse image of $H\cup M$ is the union of the exceptional hyperplane $t_j=0$ and the strict transforms [def-nagata-strict-transform] of the components $V(t_i)$, $i\in I$. On this chart the strict transform of $V(t_i)$ is the coordinate hyperplane $u_i=0$ if $i\in J\setminus\{j\}$, is empty if $i=j$, and is the coordinate hyperplane $t_i=0$ if $i\notin J$. Scheme-theoretic intersections and codimension use [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: Order the elements of J with j first. The regular-parameter node [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] applies after this permutation: the sequence (t_j,(t_i)_{i\in J\{j}}) is regular, and R/(t_i:i\in J) is regular local. The chart presentation is the specialization of [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] with a=t_j and a_i=t_i. Its quotient by t_j is (R/(t_i:i\in J))[u_i\mid i\in J\{j}], which is regular by [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base] and the regular-local-to-regular-ring consequence in [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Multiplication by t_j on the chart is injective by the closed chart-generator lemma [lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]. If a prime P does not contain t_j, the chart localization is the corresponding localization of R and is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. If P contains t_j, localize at P and apply [lem-exc-regular-local-lift-regular-sequence-quotient] to the nonzerodivisor t_j and the regular quotient just described. Thus every chart local ring is regular.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: On the chart, the pullback of t_i is t_j for i=j, t_j u_i for i in J\{j}, and t_i for i not in J. The chart extended center ideal is (t_j) by [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal]. Therefore the pullback of t_1\cdots t_r has support exactly the union of t_j=0, u_i=0 for i in (J\{j})\cap\{1,\ldots,r\}, and t_k=0 for k\le r with k not in J. Passing to the reduction removes nilpotents but preserves this support by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], and the equations define closed immersions by [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: Fix a prime P and a selected subset of the displayed hyperplanes. A listed equation that is a unit at P gives an empty local intersection. For the remaining equations, first consider P with t_j not in P: the chart is a localization of R, and the surviving u_i equations are associates of t_i because t_i=t_j u_i; the selected t_i and t_k classes are independent members of the cotangent basis supplied by the permuted parameter system. If t_j is in P, the chart relations give t_i=t_j u_i: when u_i is in P this term is in the square of the maximal ideal, and when u_i is a unit t_i is an associate of t_j. Hence the classes of the vanishing coordinates t_j, the u_i in P, and the t_k in P with k not in J are linearly independent in the cotangent space; extend them to a minimal generating set of the maximal ideal. The resulting regular system of parameters is a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. Quotienting successively by the selected equations therefore leaves a regular local ring and lowers dimension by one for each equation; localization is covered by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Thus each nonempty intersection is regular and has codimension equal to the number of selected hyperplanes, with codimension interpreted by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 proof and Remark 4.2.2(i), printed pp. 118, 121

proof.text: Use the strict-transform closure definition [def-nagata-strict-transform] with the complement of the center. On the j-chart the extended center ideal is (t_j) by [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal], so the part away from the center is D(t_j). For i=j, the relation t_i=t_j u_i forces every point with t_j=0 on V(t_j) to lie over the center, hence the chart contribution to the strict transform is empty. For i in J\{j}, on D(t_j) the equation t_i=0 is equivalent to u_i=0; its closure is V(u_i), because t_j is a nonzerodivisor on A_j/(u_i) by [lem-trf-chart-coordinate-nonzerodivisors]. For i not in J, the equation remains t_i=0 on D(t_j), and its closure is V(t_i), because t_j is a nonzerodivisor on A_j/(t_i) by the same node. Reduction and the closed-immersion interpretation are supplied by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] and [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: The standard charts are charts of one blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup], so the local descriptions agree on overlaps. Steps 2 and 3 give the reduced coordinate union and all scheme-theoretic intersections; Step 4 gives the exceptional component and each strict transform. If I is empty, H is empty and only the exceptional hyperplane remains. This proves the asserted chartwise statement, including the empty-product case.
